description.ncbi_summary: CpG methylation is an epigenetic modification that is important for embryonic development, imprinting, and X-chromosome inactivation. Studies in mice have demonstrated that DNA methylation is required for mammalian development. This gene encodes a nuclear protein with similarity to DNA methyltransferases, but is not thought to function as a DNA methyltransferase as it does not contain the amino acid residues necessary for methyltransferase activity. However, it does stimulate de novo methylation by DNA cytosine methyltransferase 3 alpha and is thought to be required for the establishment of maternal genomic imprints. This protein also mediates transcriptional repression through interaction with histone deacetylase 1. Alternatively spliced transcript variants encoding different isoforms have been found for this gene. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2012].

uniprot_function.text: Catalytically inactive regulatory factor of DNA methyltransferases DNMT3A and DNMT3B, which promotes de novo DNA methylation in embryonic stem cells and germ cells (PubMed:16829525, PubMed:17687327, PubMed:20838592, PubMed:25383530, PubMed:27121154, PubMed:29414941, PubMed:41174279, PubMed:41708613). Acts by forming a heterotetramer with DNA methyltransferase DNMT3A or DNMT3B, which induces conformational changes that open the DNA methyltransferase active site, accelerating its binding to DNA and S-adenosyl-L-methionine, and significantly enhancing its methylation efficiency (PubMed:16829525, PubMed:17687327, PubMed:25383530, PubMed:41708613). DNMT3L also acts as a histone reader, promoting association with nucleosomes and promoting recruitment of the DNA methyltransferase complex to chromatin (PubMed:41174279). Specifically recognizes unmethylated histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me0) (PubMed:17687327). In contrast, interaction is strongly inhibited by methylation at lysine 4 (H3K4me) (PubMed:17687327). DNMT3L is also required to mitigate the impact of the intrinsic DNMT3A/DNMT3B sequence preference by providing a greater boost to the methylation of poorly methylated sites, thereby promoting the formation of broader and more uniform methylation patterns (PubMed:20838592). Plays a key role in embryonic stem cells and germ cells together with isoform DNMT3A2 of DNMT3A (By similarity). In germ cells, required for the methylation of imprinted loci together with DNMT3A (By similarity). In male germ cells, specifically required to methylate retrotransposons, preventing their mobilization (By similarity). Can also act as an inhibitor of DNA methylation in some case: antaginizes DNA methylation at the promoter of bivalent genes, allowing these genes to remain in a poised, unmethylated state (By similarity). Promotes differentiation of ESCs into primordial germ cells by inhibiting DNA methylation at the promoter of RHOX5, thereby activating its expression (By similarity). Interacts with the EZH2 component of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, preventing interaction of DNMT3A and DNMT3B with the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, leading to maintain low methylation levels at the promoters of bivalent genes (By similarity).
